WITH matched_fees AS (
  SELECT f.feerate, f.rebrate, o.mktnote
  FROM fees f
  INNER JOIN orders o ON f.orderslink = o.recordvault
),
pair_averages AS (
  SELECT mktnote, AVG(feerate - rebrate) AS avg_net_fee_rate
  FROM matched_fees
  GROUP BY mktnote
),
benchmark_calc AS (
  SELECT AVG(avg_net_fee_rate) AS benchmark_value
  FROM pair_averages
),
above_benchmark_pairs AS (
  SELECT pa.avg_net_fee_rate
  FROM pair_averages pa
  WHERE pa.avg_net_fee_rate > (SELECT benchmark_value FROM benchmark_calc)
)
SELECT
  AVG(avg_net_fee_rate) AS avg_above_benchmark,
  AVG(avg_net_fee_rate) - (SELECT benchmark_value FROM benchmark_calc) AS avg_excess
FROM above_benchmark_pairs

assumptions.assumption: orders.recordvault is unique (or at least that each fee's orderslink matches at most one order). The documentation describes it as a 'unique order reference', supporting this interpretation. If not, fees matching multiple orders would be counted multiple times in the grouping.

When no trading pairs exceed the benchmark, the query returns a single row with NULL values for both columns. The request specifies 'return a single row', and this is the natural outcome when the filtered set is empty.
